run.description: Run a shell command on the device and return stdout, stderr, and exit_code. Pipes, redirects, and && chains work. A Mac endpoint executes through the signed-in user's login shell (`zsh -l -c`), so host-installed CLIs (gh, git, bun, brew, …) resolve via PATH; a headless endpoint executes through `bash --noprofile --norc -c`, which loads no profile or rc file, so prefer absolute paths over aliases there. Prefer one focused command per call over a long script. Destructive/open-world by nature — gate with approval in production.

command.description: Shell command to execute. Keep commands short and targeted.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory. Defaults to the user's home directory. Must exist.

stdin.description: Optional string piped to the command's stdin.

timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock budget in milliseconds. On timeout the process gets SIGTERM (3s grace) then SIGKILL. Default 60000, max 150000.

run.name: Run command

description: Run shell commands on this device through Lobu. Returns structured stdout/stderr/exit_code. Same trust tier as computer use — commands see the device's real filesystem and PATH. On a Mac they run as the signed-in user in that user's environment; on a headless host they run in a minimal environment with no profile and no inherited secrets. Gate with approval.
name: Shell
